reuse_profiles.definition: An adult fictional character keeps a controlled social presentation while a small contained affect leak and one interrupted self-regulation or connection gesture become simultaneously visible.

render_gates.description: The fictional subject is visibly adult and retains the identity and role supplied by the requester.
Grooming, posture, and facial baseline retain a carefully controlled public-facing surface.
A restrained affect leak is visibly readable around the eyes, mouth, or breath without melodramatic collapse.
One interrupted self-regulation or connection gesture is visibly unfinished rather than merely described.
Controlled surface, affect leak, and interrupted gesture coexist on the same character in the same moment.
The image reads as a specific three-part affective contradiction, not merely gothic fashion, a sad gaze, or a decorative prop.
The user's requested role, fashion, and reference-face use remain intact and are not replaced by the affective profile.

reuse_profiles.definition: A context-bound positive display immediately after the same adult visibly completes or verifies a difficult task, combining a readable successful outcome with a mostly symmetric smile, attention to the result, and a post-success action consequence; it does not prove a hidden or genuine emotional state.

render_gates.description: The adult's successful task result is visibly readable without relying on prompt text or a caption.
Both lip corners and cheeks show a mostly symmetric positive facial action rather than a one-sided smirk.
Iris direction and body orientation remain tied to the completed result or the collaborator sharing it, not the camera or viewer.
The result, a visibly released or open hand separated from the completed control, and the reaction compose an immediately-after-success event; continued operation is not a post-success consequence.

reuse_profiles.definition: A restrained relationship-directed smile used while one adult performs a concrete supportive action toward a visibly concerned adult peer, with mutual orientation and an observable easing or acceptance response; the cues show an interaction function, not sincerity, consent, trustworthiness, or personality.

render_gates.description: Both adult participants and their mutual or shared-target orientation remain legible in the same frame.
The main adult shows a small bilateral closed or lip-pressed smile rather than a broad victory grin or smirk.
A concrete repair, return, steadying, or handoff action visibly explains the relationship-directed display.
The adult peer visibly accepts, eases, or reciprocally orients so the interaction has an observable consequence.

reuse_profiles.definition: A visible pre-decision display in which an adult compares at least two readable alternatives, the still-frame eyeline lands on one alternative while head or tool geometry keeps both in active comparison, slight brow or mouth tension accompanies a paused hand or tool, and the choice remains unresolved; no single face action is treated as proof of confusion.

render_gates.description: Two distinct and comparable physical alternatives are simultaneously visible and remain clearly separate.
The irises visibly land on one alternative while head angle or paused-tool geometry keeps both alternatives in active comparison; impossible simultaneous split gaze and unrelated fixation both fail.
Restrained brow asymmetry or knitting and mild mouth tension support comparison without becoming an exaggerated cartoon face.
A hand, pen, or tool is visibly paused before either alternative is selected.
The whole frame reads as an unresolved comparison rather than completed selection, inspection, skepticism, or failure.

reuse_profiles.definition: A short social-repair sequence after an adult causes a minor, non-harmful, visible mishap: the adult briefly breaks gaze or lowers the head, shows a small closed smile or face-touch cue, performs concrete restitution, and receives an observable peer response; the display is not a moral or personality diagnosis.

render_gates.description: A minor non-harmful mishap and its affected objects remain visibly identifiable in the scene.
A brief gaze or head break and restrained closed smile or face-touch cue are photographically readable without exaggerated cartoon symbols.
The adult visibly gathers, reorders, wipes, replaces, or returns what the mishap disrupted.
An adult peer visibly helps, accepts, or signals that the small social rupture is being repaired.

reuse_profiles.definition: A post-verification release display after an adult checks a previously uncertain but non-graphic safety condition and receives visible evidence that a person, system, or route is safe, combining the verification action with loosened shoulders, jaw or eyelids and an immediate practical consequence; face alone does not establish relief.

render_gates.description: A non-graphic alarm, warning residue, stopped machine, or blocked route makes the prior uncertainty visually legible.
The main adult's pupils and face visibly align with the gauge, signal, route, or colleague being checked; a second person pointing while the main adult reads unrelated paperwork does not count.
At least two channels among shoulders, jaw, eyelids, and gripping hand visibly loosen together rather than reading as generic fatigue, calm, or checklist concentration.
Lowering the emergency tool or resuming the safe task makes the display read as after confirmation rather than calm before an unknown outcome.
